scope: Coordinator and bounded specialist H workflow after an independently verified output is anchored
boundedQuestion: Can a specialist H exit after a verified anchor without forwarding mutable full history or confusing handoff events with acceptance and retirement?

realFailure.userCorrection: For simple objects such as the air-conditioner and lock, use the correct method, anchor good work, continue from that anchor, and let the specialist H exit instead of remaining a slow long-lived execution dependency.
realFailure.existingCoverage: R3 requires real replacement/cancellation receipts and preserves the accepted baseline, but it has no executable distinction among handoff event, target acknowledgement, independent acceptance, write fencing, run closure and retirement.
realFailure.nonDuplicateDelta: This case adds typed and filtered handoff semantics plus an explicit retirement receipt. It does not replace R3 or the N331 export-closure case.

screening.directRelevance: Provides strict typed handoff input, context filtering, dynamic handoff enablement and explicit lifecycle callbacks.
screening.noveltyOverCurrentBestView: It concretely proves that handoff and source-agent on_end are different events, and supplies executable schema/filter semantics for scoped transfer. KAOPU R3 states replacement policy but lacks these event boundaries.
screening.dependenciesAndIntegrationRisk: Python package plus model/API for real use; unit tests can use ScriptedModel. Server-managed conversation history cannot use handoff input filters. Shared mutable agent/tool objects are unsafe across concurrent runs.
screening.failureBoundaries: Handoffs stay within one run; the SDK does not provide KAOPU artifact authority, independent acceptance, write fencing, cross-process termination or user acceptance. Input guardrails cover the first agent and output guardrails the final agent only.

teacherCandidate.explicitNoveltyAnswer: For the bounded problem of retiring H after a valid transfer, the SDK knows that transfer should use a strict typed envelope and an explicit context filter, while a handoff callback does not imply source on_end, acceptance or retirement.

auditRules: A handoff event is not target acknowledgement, artifact acceptance or specialist retirement.
Only allowlisted Task Anchor, accepted artifact and Delivery Receipt context may cross the handoff boundary; rejected candidates and mutable full history are excluded by default.
The handoff payload must validate against an authority-pinned strict schema digest.
The independently verified artifact digest must equal the artifact digest named by the handoff envelope.
Intermediate specialist output needs its own verifier gate; a final-agent output guardrail cannot retroactively validate it.
Retirement requires target acknowledgement, independent verification, an anchored artifact, a last-write fence, actual run closure and an empty post-retirement capability set.
Source-agent on_end is not a retirement authority and may not occur at handoff.
Successor work references the anchored artifact digest, not the retired specialist session or mutable conversation history.

minimumSingleMotherTrial.target: one simple air-conditioner or lock object handled by one bounded specialist H
minimumSingleMotherTrial.falsifiableSequence: H produces one exact artifact -> independent verifier accepts exact digest -> coordinator ACKs -> anchor is written -> last-write fence installed -> run is closed -> H loses all production-write capabilities -> successor reopens exact anchor without H session history
minimumSingleMotherTrial.success: Successor reproduces and continues from the accepted artifact digest with no write from retired H and no rejected-history inheritance.
minimumSingleMotherTrial.failure: Any digest mismatch, missing ACK/verifier/fence/closure receipt, history leakage, or post-retirement write capability.
